landing_ground_roll_provenance.title: Landing Distance - Short Field
landing_ground_roll_provenance.conditions: Flaps 30 deg, power off, maximum braking, paved level dry runway, zero wind
notes: Short field technique as specified in Section 4.
Decrease distances 10% for each 9 knots headwind. For operation with tailwinds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2 knots.
For operation on a dry, grass runway, increase distances by 45% of the "ground roll" figure.

stall_speeds_provenance.title: Stall Speeds
stall_speeds_provenance.conditions: Power off, 1670 lb, most rearward and most forward center of gravity
notes: Altitude loss during a stall recovery may be as much as 160 feet.
KIAS values are approximate and are based on airspeed calibration data with power off.
stall_speeds_provenance.note: Figure 5-3, printed page 5-10, dated 1 July 1978, PDF page 73. The figure prints two blocks at 1670 lb, MOST REARWARD CENTER OF GRAVITY above MOST FORWARD CENTER OF GRAVITY, and both are carried, in page order. A scan has no text layer to read a block's C.G. label from, so each block is its own clipped sheet and the sheet names its C.G. (sheets[].cg, stamped by extract.stamp_sheet_row, which refuses a label the page contradicts). Clips: rearward [10, 238, 352, 372], forward [10, 405.75, 352, 535] (unchanged), each one full-frame pass at zoom 6 (strip_pt wider than the clip, so each value is one token) and rotate 360, a full turn that changes nothing in the image but makes ocr.py report coordinates relative to the clip. With the scanned stall guards (lines grouped by the gaps between words; a header word found inside a token that swallowed a ruled line; a cell refused unless both KIAS and KCAS read and nothing else reads under the same column), each clip edge was swept on 2026-09-28 with the other edges as set: rearward top 228 to 250 pt in 0.25 pt steps, 88 of 89 read all 24 values correctly and 1 refuses; rearward bottom 364 to 386 in 0.5 pt steps, 45 of 45; forward top 398 to 410 in 0.25 pt steps, 48 of 49 and 1 refuses; forward bottom 529 to 540, 23 of 23. No edge returned a wrong or missing value (backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/c152/pipeline/sweeps_stall.txt). The forward block is the higher of the two at every flap and bank setting (4 to 6 KIAS, 2 to 4 KCAS), so it is the conservative one. Proof, every one of the 48 values against the rendered page: backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/c152/pipeline/proof_stall_speeds.py.

time_fuel_distance_to_climb_provenance.title: Time, Fuel, and Distance to Climb - Maximum Rate of Climb
time_fuel_distance_to_climb_provenance.conditions: Flaps up, full throttle, standard temperature
notes: Add 0.8 of a gallon of fuel for engine start, taxi and takeoff allowance.
Mixture leaned above 3000 feet for maximum RPM.
Increase time, fuel and distance by 10% for each 10 C above standard temperature.
Distances shown are based on zero wind.
time_fuel_distance_to_climb_provenance.note: Figure 5-6, printed page 5-13, dated 1 July 1978, PDF page 76 (upright). Read with the scanned row-table guards (extract.extract_row_table on a scan: an altitude label read twice is one row and each block's labels must climb by one constant step; fuel_gal is declared the decimal column and the page must agree, and a token of the other shape is dropped; a cell whose passes disagree or that no pass read is re-read alone or refused; each column must run the declared way from sea level and within 5 times its median step, or its cells are re-read and otherwise refused). The TEMP column is counted but not published (drop_fields): it is the standard temperature for each altitude, which the conditions already state, and a scanned '- 1' reads as '1'. Settings: clip [45, 300, 385, 505] (the 13 data rows, below the column headings), rotate 360, zoom 4, strips 90/30. Of 60 settings swept on 2026-09-28 (zoom 3 to 6, five strip widths, with and without the clip) 5 read every cell correctly and 55 refuse; none returned a wrong number. All 65 published values proven against the rendered page: backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/c152/pipeline/proof_time_fuel_distance_to_climb.txt.

provenance.notes: CG envelope corrected to TCDS 3A19 Model 152: forward limit was a near-flat 31.0-32.0 (up to ~0.65 in more nose-heavy-permissive than certified at gross) -> certified taper 31.0@<=1350 / 32.65@1670 (moves AFT/holds = more restrictive); aft limit 40.5 was 4.0 in TOO PERMISSIVE AFT -> certified constant 36.5 (moves FORWARD = more restrictive). Both changes are SAFE DIRECTION. Station arms de-contaminated to certified: front_seats_arm 37.0->39.0 (TCDS '2 at +39'), fuel_arm 37.5->42.0 (TCDS 'two 13 gal tanks at +42.0'), baggage_arm 80.0->64.0 (POH Baggage Area 1 main compartment; Area 2 child seat is ~+84, not modeled in a single station). rear_seats_arm null CORRECT (2-place). empty_weight_arm 36.5 UNCHANGED (TCDS Empty Weight C.G. Range: None -> no certified empty-CG arm; not invented per Hard Constraint). FLAG: the 36.5 placeholder sits exactly on the certified aft limit 36.5 (passes the inclusive in-envelope lint at the boundary) and is implausibly aft for a real empty 152 (~31-33 in) -> replace with a genuine empty CG in the Track-B slice that owns the data_version bump + iOS regen (empty_weight_arm is drift-coupled). NOT changed this slice (drift-coupled, Track B): usable_fuel_gal 24.5, empty_weight 1080. Full findings: docs/fd-419-s3-cessna-singles-wb-findings-2026-07-26.md.
